knowledge_point.title: Finding the Midline of a Transformed Sinusoidal Function

question.:question/problem: Find the equation of the midline for a transformed sine function with a minimum value of $-14$ and a maximum value of $-5.$
question.:question/worked-solution:
A sinusoidal graph's midline (or vertical shift) is the horizontal line that divides it vertically in half. 

The equation of the midline is given by

$$
y=\frac{{y}_{\text{min}}+{y}_{\text{max}}}{2},
$$

where ${y}_{\text{min}}$ and ${y}_{\text{max}}$ are the minimum and maximum values of the function. The midline equals the average of the maximum and minimum values. 

In our case, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{{y}_{\text{min}}+{y}_{\text{max}}}{2} & =\frac{-14+(-5)}{2} \\  & =\frac{-19}{2} \\  & =- \frac{19}{2}.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the midline is $y=- \frac{19}{2}.$
